newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-BRITONS ROAR APPROVAL FOR "PEOPLE'S SUNDAY".
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BRITONS ROAR APPROVAL FOR "PEOPLE'S SUNDAY".

text.p: The walls of centre court shook as British tennis-lovers, who descended on Wimbledon in droves on Sunday were gripped by "Henmania".
Deprived of a real British contender for the title for so many years, fans roared their approval as Tim Henman, seeded 14, began his third round match against Paul Haarhuis of the Netherlands.
"It's totally mad," said one official as the crowd chanted "Henman, Henman."
During the warm-up, they cheered the Briton's every shot, and even Princess Michael of Kent joined in the rowdy Mexican wave.
"It's great for British tennis," said one fan eagerly awaiting Henman's clash.

For only the second time in history the gates were open on the middle Sunday of the tournament. Tickets for centre court and number one court were offered for 15 pounds ($25), while ground passes were on sale for five pounds.
Thousands of hopeful enthusiasts were still queuing outside, keen to witness some long-awaited British success or just see a few famous names.
After Henman, there was Greg Rusedski playing fellow Briton Andrew Richardson on Number One Court.
Earlier, John McEnroe took his seat among the already buzzing centre court crowd and whipped them to further frenzy with the ever-popular Mexican wave.
But some of the 21,000 centre court and number one court ticket holders abandoned their cherished seats to see some well-known tennis faces on the outside courts.
"We're on centre court, but we wanted to see Novotna," said Jan Taylor from Watford. "She always falls to pieces."
Jana Novotna, seeded number three, almost did fall to pieces and dropped a set to Russian Elena Likhovtseva, before eventually showing her mettle to clinch the third set 6-4.
Czech Novotna is already a people's favourite after famously sobbing on the shoulder of the Duchess of Kent after she lost the 1993 final to Steffi Graf.
Helena Sukova was another veteran who prized spectators away from the show courts when she briskly saw off ex-champion Conchita Martinez in two sets.
"I recognised the names so I thought I'd come and have a look," said one avid tennis fan who had travelled up from Southampton early this morning.
Flasks of tea and packed lunches replaced the traditional fare of Pimms and champagne and strawberries and cream and the members' enclosure looked decidedly bare.
"We've eaten most of what we had in the queue," said Virginia Barker from Berkshire.
But Christian Brown from Colchester, who queued since 8.30 this morning for his centre court ticket, was determined to sample as many Wimbledon traditions as possible.
"It's a great atmosphere -- So friendly and open. I've had Pimms and strawberries but I can't afford the champagne," he said, before dashing off to cheer Henman.
